## 2024-10-07 - requests Exception Credential Leakage & URL Encoding
**Vulnerability:** Proxy credentials (passwords and usernames) were logged in plaintext in standard output, and they were also exposed in raw exception messages generated by the `requests` library when connections failed. Furthermore, credentials were not URL-encoded when constructing the proxy URL, making it vulnerable to injection-like errors if special characters (like `@` or `:`) were present in passwords.
**Learning:** External libraries like `requests` often include request details (including complete proxy URLs with credentials) in their stringified exception objects. Printing raw exceptions directly without sanitization can inadvertently leak secrets to logs or the console.
**Prevention:** Always parse or split sensitive strings to isolate and mask credentials before logging. When handling exceptions in network requests, avoid printing raw exception objects; instead, sanitize error messages using regex to mask passwords while preserving debugging context. Additionally, always use URL-encoding (e.g., `urllib.parse.quote`) when interpolating credentials into a URL structure.
